epic.intent:
Add **Dark Mechanicus** to the Coding Reference page on davgor.github.io: a project card with accurate copy and real app screenshots, plus a **read-only plan view rendered from this epic's own saved plan** in `.darkmechanicus/`. Visitors see a real Dark Mechanicus plan, the one that delivered the section they are reading, not a mockup.

**Who benefits:** visitors and reviewers of the portfolio, who get a concrete look at how the agentic planning and execution flow works.

**Out of scope:** running Dark Mechanicus in the browser, any live MCP or network connection, editing plans from the site, other epics' plans, and changes to the DarkMechanicus repository itself.

successCriteria.text: Coding Reference shows a Dark Mechanicus project card whose first-person copy matches what v0.8.0 actually ships (MCP server + desktop app on shared repository-owned state, draft -> Save -> orchestrated run, human-approved sprint checkpoints) and links to the GitHub repo and its latest release.
The card includes 2-3 real desktop-app screenshots with descriptive alt text, none showing a private repository name, local path, username, or session/machine id.

The page renders a read-only plan view of this epic's own saved plan: sprints in order with goals, every ticket's display key, title and status, and every dependency edge, with an accessible text equivalent.

The plan view's data is generated from committed .darkmechanicus/ records at dev/build time, with no Dark Mechanicus install, through an allowlist that excludes paths, ids, ticket bodies, references and comments; the same records always produce byte-identical output.

Existing Coding Reference content (Fantasy World Generator showcase and project cards) still renders, and lint, format:check, test:unit, fireguard (no F), type-check, deadcode, build and test:e2e pass.

The change is merged to main via a PR with a posted red-team review, the Pages deploy succeeds, and https://davgor.github.io/coding-reference shows the card and plan view at desktop width and at 375px with no page-level horizontal scroll.

bundle.rationale:
**Shape.** Three human-checkpointed sprints, following the layout the person chose: content (copy + screenshots), then data + view (export -> plan view), then ship (integrate -> release). Sprint 1's two tickets run in parallel; Sprint 2 is a strict chain because the view consumes the export's schema and fixture. DGI-5 is the integration join: Sprint 1 and Sprint 2 both touch `CodingReference.tsx` and its tests, and only there are the pieces combined and e2e-tested. DGI-6 verifies every success criterion end to end. Critical path: DGI-3 -> DGI-4 -> DGI-5 -> DGI-6.

**Assumptions (change at a checkpoint if wrong):**
- The card sits directly after the Fantasy World Generator showcase.
- The plan view shows *this* epic only, by configured id, with statuses as of the committed records. The live page lags by one commit after the epic completes.
- The export reads committed `.darkmechanicus/` JSON. `.darkmechanicus/` is currently untracked, and committing it is the person's call (Sprint 2 entry criterion).
- Screenshots need the desktop GUI. If no worker has it, the person captures the raw images (DGI-2 says how to ask).
- Prefer a dependency-free graph rendering to keep the bundle and the `npm audit` surface small.
- No epic feature branch was named. Set one before the run starts (suggested: `epic/dark-mechanicus-showcase`); otherwise the run binds the current checkout branch.
- Merging to main (DGI-6) is outward-facing and waits for the person's explicit go-ahead.

**Process.** Every implementation ticket follows this repo's delivery standards: TDD-first, the full gate, and fireguard on new tests. DGI-6 carries the mandatory red-team review.

tickets.body:
Add a `BlogCard` for **Dark Mechanicus** to `src/pages/CodingReference.tsx`, following the BoosterSeat card pattern (board ticket 018).

**Copy:** first person, matching the voice of the existing cards, 3-4 paragraphs. Source every claim from the DarkMechanicus README and docs at v0.8.0. Cover:
- what it is: local planning and execution coordination for agentic development, with an MCP server for agents and an Electron desktop app for people, both operating on the same repository-owned state under the same rules;
- the flow: an agent drafts an epic, a person reviews the plan graph and presses **Save**, then an orchestrator runs the saved revision, claims ready tickets and stops at each sprint checkpoint for human approval;
- the design choices worth showing an engineer: the server enforces the rules, roles are fixed at launch, plans are Git-tracked JSON under `.darkmechanicus/` while the SQLite working database stays local, and agents can run with the desktop closed;
- stack and release: Electron, React, TypeScript, `node:sqlite`, MCP SDK, React Flow, zod; Win + Mac builds with auto-update.

**Placement (assumption):** directly after the Fantasy World Generator showcase section. The person can move it at the Sprint 1 checkpoint.

**Links:** `https://github.com/davgor/DarkMechanicus` and `https://github.com/davgor/DarkMechanicus/releases/latest`. Use `/latest` rather than pinning a version, so the link does not go stale.

**Out of scope:** screenshots (DGI-2), the plan view (Sprint 2), and wiring images into the card (DGI-5).

**TDD:** write the CodingReference unit tests first and watch them fail.

tickets.body:
Add a dev/build-time export that reads this repository's committed Dark Mechanicus portable records and emits a static, sanitized plan JSON for the site.

**Input** (formats documented in DarkMechanicus `docs/architecture.md`, "Portable records"):
- `.darkmechanicus/epics/<epicId>/current.json`: `darkmechanicus.epic-pointer` v1, with `revisionId`.
- `.darkmechanicus/epics/<epicId>/snapshots/<revisionId>.json`: the plan bundle, containing `epic`, `sprints[]` (ordinal, goal, exitCriteria, ticketIds), `tickets[]` (id, key, title, optional) and `edges[]` (from, to).
- `.darkmechanicus/epics/<epicId>/state.json`: `darkmechanicus.epic-state` v1, with `status` and `ticketStatuses`.

**Which epic:** a configured epic id (this epic, `ep_01m3tyvkcv6kzg24j40g1mzh87`) in one small config constant. Not "latest" and not "all".

**Output: allowlist only, never a denylist.** Epic title, success-criteria text, epic status, revision number and saved-at date; sprints (ordinal, goal, exit criteria); tickets (display key, title, sprint ordinal, status, optional flag); edges by display key. **Excluded:** ticket bodies, references, capability profiles, comments, branch/commit data, run history, and all project/machine/session/run ids.

**Mechanism (recommended):** a pure-Node module under `scripts/` plus a small Vite plugin, so `npm run dev` (which Playwright uses, port 5175), `npm run build` and CI all serve `/darkmechanicus/plan.json`. The output is generated, not committed. Unit tests use a committed fixture copied from real records, with poisoned values (paths, ids, bodies) added to prove the allowlist. Another mechanism is fine if it meets every criterion; record why in the submission.

**Failure:** fail loudly with a message naming the file when records are missing, when `format`/`formatVersion` is unknown, when the pointer's snapshot is missing, or when an edge names an unknown ticket. The site must never silently ship an empty plan.

**Determinism:** stable key order, sorted where order is not meaningful, no export-time timestamps.

**Docs:** add a README section on how the plan view is generated and how to point it at another epic.

**Entry precondition:** this epic's `.darkmechanicus/` records are committed (see the Sprint 2 entry criteria).

tickets.body:
A React component that renders the exported plan from DGI-3.

**Layout:** sprints in order as columns, each headed by its ordinal and goal. Each ticket is a node showing display key, title and a status label. Dependency edges are drawn between nodes. The component is read-only: no buttons or affordances that imply editing or running anything.

**Rendering approach:** prefer dependency-free (CSS grid + inline SVG edges). A graph library needs a written justification in the submission, must be lazy-loaded, and must keep `npm audit` clean.

**Accessibility:** provide an equivalent structured text list ("Sprint 2 · DGI-4 Build the read-only plan view, status: ready, requires DGI-3"), so all information is available without seeing the edges. Status must be conveyed by text as well as color, and nothing traps keyboard focus.

**Theme:** use the site's existing CSS tokens in `src/index.css` for light/dark.

**Narrow screens:** below 768px, sprints stack vertically. At 375px the page must not scroll horizontally; the component may scroll internally.

**Data loading:** fetch the JSON served by DGI-3, with loading and error states. A failed or malformed fetch shows a short plain message and never breaks the rest of the page.

**Tests:** use DGI-3's fixture.

**Out of scope:** embedding in Coding Reference (DGI-5).

tickets.body:
Final end-to-end ticket. Every epic success criterion is verified here.

1. **Open the PR:** from the epic branch to `main`. Include the `.darkmechanicus/` records the export needs; the person approved committing them at Sprint 2.
2. **Red-team review:** per `.claude/skills/red-team-review/SKILL.md`, posted on the PR with `<!-- red-team-review -->`. Fix every Blocking finding and re-run the gate.
3. **Merge:** only after all PR checks are green **and the person gives a go-ahead in chat**. Merging is outward-facing.
4. **Deploy:** confirm the GitHub Pages deploy for the merge commit succeeded, including the production HTML smoke check.
5. **Verify live:** check https://davgor.github.io/coding-reference at desktop width and at 375px for the card, links, screenshots and plan view, with no console errors and no page-level horizontal scroll.
6. **Report:** map each epic success criterion (s1-s6) to evidence: PR URL, merge SHA, deploy run URL, command output and screenshots.

**Known limitation to state in the sprint report:** the live plan view shows ticket statuses as of the merged records. This ticket and the epic's completion only appear there after the person commits the final `.darkmechanicus/` state and it deploys. No code change is needed for that.
